thread:
oncall-bot: PAGER: high tail-latency detected for dedicated tenant 'atlasmed-prod' (pool: dedicated-usw2-3). 95p latency spiking ~2.4s, baseline ~0.35s. Alert: /alerts/atlasmed-dedicated-tail (pagerduty triggered) :rotating_light:

sara: I'm on it — taking the ticket. First check: any customer-facing 5xx/timeout spikes?

devon: seeing a lot of long requests (huge prompts) piling into the scheduler. Batch sizes blow out because client sometimes sends huge embed+context sequences. Sample of recent requests: tokens ~28k, 35k, 41k. That saturates KV cache and causes long serialization.

sara: ack. Is this new traffic pattern or something recent on our side?

carmen: customer reported a heavy ingestion job this morning — could be a migration hitting prod. No code deploys on runtime in the last 6h.

tony: GPU pool metrics: GPU util steady ~65%, but scheduler queue length for atlasmed-prod jumped to 450 -> backlog. Token-based batching means a few giant requests force smaller requests to wait. Also seeing worker heartbeats delayed (~8s).

sara: probable mitigation path: 1) reduce tenant max_batch_tokens to bound per-batch compute, 2) switch scheduler to latency-first for this tenant, 3) apply short burst caps so a single tenant can't hold the entire shard. Will try targeted config patch.

devon: +1. We should avoid global changes. Do per-tenant config, canary to 10% hosts then 100%.

sara: proposed payload (will run via admin API). If we need rollback just reapply original values.

```json
{
  "tenant_id": "atlasmed-prod",
  "overrides": {
    "max_batch_tokens": 512,
    "scheduler_policy": "latency_first",
    "burst_limit": 20,
    "max_concurrent_requests": 80
  }
}
```

ops-bot: NOTE: admin API requires X-Admin-Token header. Rate limit applies to config changes (10/s).

sara: applying canary to 2 hosts now (dedicated-usw2-3-0, -1). Command: 

```bash
curl -X PATCH "https://internal-console.redwood/api/v1/tenants/atlasmed-prod/config"
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"overrides":{"max_batch_tokens":512,"scheduler_policy":"latency_first","burst_limit":20}}'
```

sara: canary applied to -0 and -1. Watching metrics: https://grafana.redwood/atlasmed/dedicated-pool (link)

devon: initial observation: tail latency for requests routed to canary hosts dropped from ~2.3s to ~0.45s for 95p. Good sign. Throughput per-host slightly down but overall service latency improves.

tony: also added an ephemeral token-length shedder to reject >50k token requests with 413 to protect pool — this is a temporary policy change at the router layer (will rollback once customer finishes migration).

sara: customer impact: they saw errors/timeouts for ~24m before mitigations, estimate 4% of their requests got 5xx/timeout. Informed account team (cc @carmen).

li: I'll take the handoff once we stabilize. Current plan for handoff: leave per-tenant overrides in place for 2h, monitor 95p and 99p every 5m, if stable for 30m start gradual easing: max_batch_tokens -> 1024, burst_limit -> 40.

sara: agreed. Creating runbook entry in incident doc, tagging this thread to incident ticket PD-12345.

```text
Runbook snippet:
- Apply per-tenant overrides (canary -> 2 hosts)
- Monitor metrics: 95p latency, worker heartbeats, backlog
- If tail drops -> expand to 100% hosts (rolling)
- If regress -> rollback to previous config
- Temporary router-level shed: reject >50k tokens
```

ops-bot: DEPLOY-BOT: rolled override to remaining hosts (rolling, 20s per host).

devon: After full rollout: 95p latency for atlasmed-prod is 0.48s (was 2.4s), backlog back to normal. No new worker errors.

sara: leaving overrides for 2h and then will start easing per li's plan. Carmen, please coordinate with AtlasMed account to pause the ingestion job if they can to avoid repeated flips.

carmen: pinged AtlasMed CSM and engineering. They acknowledged and will throttle ingestion in next 30m.

li: taking over on-call at 22:00 UTC — will watch dashboards and be ready to rollback. Handoff notes saved to incident PD-12345.

sara: thanks team. Postmortem to follow once incident closed. :white_check_mark:
